subject: science
prompt_en: Railway tracks are made of iron and steel and stay outdoors in the rain. The tops of the rails look shiny, but their sides look rusty. Why might that be?
prompt_hi: Railway ki patriyan lohe aur steel ki hoti hain aur baarish mein bahar padi rehti hain. Patri ka upar wala hissa chamakdaar dikhta hai, par side jung lagi dikhti hai. Aisa kyon?
answer: Train wheels keep rubbing the top of the rails, scraping off any rust as soon as it forms and keeping the metal shiny; the sides are not rubbed, so the rust stays there.

subject: science
prompt_en: Neha says, 'Rust is only dust that sticks to wet iron, so just wipe it off and the gate is as good as new.' What is the mistake?
prompt_hi: Neha kehti hai, 'Jung bas dhool hai jo geele lohe pe chipak jaati hai, toh bas poochh do aur gate naya jaisa ho jaayega.' Galti kya hai?
answer: Rust is a new substance formed from the iron itself reacting with oxygen and water; wiping it off removes some of the iron, so the gate is thinner and weaker, not as good as new.

subject: science
prompt_en: Draw the three-nail experiment as three cups, each labelled with whether it has air and whether it has water, and mark which nail rusts. Then say in one sentence what the drawing proves.
prompt_hi: 3-keel wala experiment 3 cup ke roop mein banao, har cup pe likho ki usmein hawa hai ya nahi aur paani hai ya nahi, aur jis keel ko jung laga use mark karo. Phir ek line mein batao drawing kya saabit karti hai.
answer: Cup with air but no water: no rust. Cup with water but no air: no rust. Cup with both air and water: rusty nail. It proves that iron needs both air and water to rust.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to your cousin why his new bicycle should be wiped dry and oiled during the monsoon.
prompt_hi: Apne cousin ko samjhao ki monsoon mein uski nayi cycle ko poochh ke sukhaana aur tel lagaana kyon zaroori hai.
answer: Iron rusts when both oxygen and water reach it, and the monsoon brings lots of water and moisture; wiping removes water, and oil makes a layer that keeps air and water away, so the cycle does not rust and weaken.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: what happens to silver anklets (payal) over time, and what happens to gold jewellery?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: chaandi ki payal ka samay ke saath kya hota hai, aur sone ke gehnon ka kya hota hai?
answer: Silver turns black (tarnishes); gold stays shiny.

subject: science
prompt_en: Pencil 'lead' is not the metal lead at all. Which non-metal is it really made of?
prompt_hi: Pencil ki 'lead' asal mein lead dhaatu nahi hai. Ye asal mein kis non-metal se bani hoti hai?
answer: Graphite, a form of carbon (mixed with clay).

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: if you open a packet of chips and leave the chips in an open bowl for two days, will they stay crisp and fresh-tasting? Then think: why are unopened packets filled with nitrogen gas instead of air?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: agar chips ka packet khol ke chips ko khuli katori mein do din chhod do, toh kya wo kurkure aur taaze rahenge? Phir socho: band packets mein hawa ki jagah nitrogen gas kyon bhari jaati hai?
answer: They go soft by taking in moisture from the air, and can taste stale because oxygen reacts with the oil in them. Nitrogen does not react with the chips, so filling the packet with it keeps out oxygen and moisture and also cushions the chips.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: if air were divided into 100 equal parts, about how many parts would be oxygen, and how many would be nitrogen?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: agar hawa ko 100 barabar hisson mein baanta jaaye, toh lagbhag kitne hisse oxygen honge aur kitne nitrogen?
answer: About 21 parts oxygen and about 78 parts nitrogen; the last 1 part is other gases such as argon and carbon dioxide.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why does a farmer add fertiliser containing nitrogen to the soil, even though the air is full of nitrogen gas?
prompt_hi: Hawa mein itni saari nitrogen gas hone ke baawajood kisaan mitti mein nitrogen wala khaad kyon daalta hai?
answer: Plants cannot use nitrogen gas from the air directly; they take in nitrogen compounds from the soil through their roots to make proteins. Fertilisers, and bacteria in the root nodules of pulse crops, supply these.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why is chlorine (or bleaching powder, which releases it) added to water in city water tanks?
prompt_hi: Shehar ki paani ki tankiyon mein chlorine (ya bleaching powder, jisse chlorine nikalti hai) kyon daali jaati hai?
answer: To kill germs in the water so that it is safe to drink.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare oxygen and nitrogen, the two main gases in air. Which one do we need for breathing and burning, and what job does the other do for plants?
prompt_hi: Hawa ki do mukhya gases, oxygen aur nitrogen, ki tulna karo. Saans lene aur jalne ke liye kaunsi chahiye, aur doosri gas paudhon ke liye kya kaam karti hai?
answer: Oxygen is needed for breathing (respiration) and for burning; nitrogen, in the form of nitrogen compounds in the soil, helps plants make proteins and grow.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why does the packet of salt in your kitchen say 'iodised'?
prompt_hi: Tumhare kitchen ke namak ke packet pe 'iodised' kyon likha hota hai?
answer: A small amount of an iodine compound is added because our body needs a little iodine; too little iodine can cause goitre, a swelling of the thyroid gland in the neck.

subject: science
prompt_en: ISRO's powerful cryogenic rocket engines burn liquid hydrogen with liquid oxygen. What do you think comes out of the exhaust, and why is hydrogen a good fuel?
prompt_hi: ISRO ke shaktishali cryogenic rocket engine liquid hydrogen ko liquid oxygen ke saath jalaate hain. Socho, exhaust se kya nikalta hoga, aur hydrogen accha fuel kyon hai?
answer: Mostly water vapour, because hydrogen combines with oxygen to form water; hydrogen gives out a very large amount of energy for its weight.

subject: science
prompt_en: Aman says, 'Non-metals are useless; we should only study metals.' Give him three examples that prove him wrong.
prompt_hi: Aman kehta hai, 'Non-metals bekaar hain, hume sirf metals padhne chahiye.' Use galat saabit karne ke liye 3 examples do.
answer: For example: oxygen for breathing and hospitals; carbon in all food and in pencil lead; nitrogen in fertilisers and chips packets; chlorine to make drinking water safe; iodine in iodised salt.

subject: science
prompt_en: Draw a 'non-metal map' of your body and home: label one place where you find oxygen, carbon, nitrogen and chlorine or iodine.
prompt_hi: Apne shareer aur ghar ka ek 'non-metal map' banao: oxygen, carbon, nitrogen aur chlorine ya iodine kahaan milte hain, har ek ki ek jagah label karo.
answer: Oxygen: in the air you breathe or a hospital cylinder. Carbon: in food, wood, a pencil or coal. Nitrogen: in air, a chips packet or fertiliser. Chlorine: in treated tap water. Iodine: in iodised salt or an antiseptic.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to your friend why life on Earth would be impossible without non-metals.
prompt_hi: Apne dost ko samjhao ki non-metals ke bina dharti pe jeevan kyon sambhav nahi hota.
answer: Living things are built mainly from non-metals such as carbon, hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen; we need oxygen to release energy from food, plants need nitrogen to make proteins, and water itself is made of hydrogen and oxygen.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: name the yellow non-metal powder used in some medicines and to make rubber stronger.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: wo peela non-metal powder kaunsa hai jo kuch dawaiyon mein aur rubber ko mazboot banane mein use hota hai?
answer: Sulphur.

subject: science
prompt_en: Give two signs that tell you a chemical change has happened.
prompt_hi: Do aise sanket batao jinse pata chale ki chemical badlav hua hai.
answer: Any two of: gas bubbles, a change of colour, heat or light given out, a new smell, a new solid forming.

subject: science
prompt_en: Put half a spoon of baking soda into a cup and add a few spoons of lemon juice or vinegar. Predict: what will you see and hear? Will it be a physical or a chemical change?
prompt_hi: Ek cup mein aadha chammach baking soda daalo aur usme kuch chammach nimbu ka ras ya sirka daalo. Guess karo: kya dikhega aur kya sunaayi dega? Ye physical badlav hoga ya chemical?
answer: It fizzes and bubbles with a hissing sound as carbon dioxide gas forms; a new substance (the gas) is made, so it is a chemical change.

subject: science
prompt_en: Weigh a glass of water on a kitchen scale, then stir in two spoons of sugar until you cannot see it. Predict: will the weight go up, stay the same or go down?
prompt_hi: Kitchen ke taraazu pe paani ka glass tolo, phir do chammach cheeni ghol do jab tak dikhe nahi. Guess karo: wazan badhega, utna hi rahega ya ghatega?
answer: It goes up by the weight of the sugar; the sugar has dissolved but it is still in the water.

subject: science
prompt_en: Ask an adult to cut an apple into two pieces. Leave one piece open on a plate and dip the other in lemon water. Predict which one turns brown faster. Is browning a physical or a chemical change?
prompt_hi: Kisi bade se seb ke do tukde katwao. Ek tukda plate pe khula chhod do aur doosre ko nimbu-paani mein dubo do. Guess karo kaunsa jaldi bhoora hoga. Bhoora hona physical badlav hai ya chemical?
answer: The open piece turns brown faster. Browning is a chemical change: substances in the apple react with oxygen in the air to make new brown substances; lemon juice slows this.

subject: science
prompt_en: Tearing a sheet of paper cannot be undone, yet it is a physical change. Why?
prompt_hi: Kaagaz phaadna ulta nahi kiya ja sakta, phir bhi ye physical badlav hai. Kyon?
answer: No new substance is formed: the torn pieces are still paper. Whether a change can be reversed is only a clue; the real test is whether a new substance forms.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare the melting of a candle's wax with the burning of its wick. Which is physical and which is chemical? Give evidence for each.
prompt_hi: Mombatti ke wax ke pighalne aur uski baati ke jalne ki tulna karo. Kaunsa physical hai aur kaunsa chemical? Dono ke liye saboot do.
answer: Melting wax is physical: the liquid wax cools back into solid wax. Burning is chemical: heat and light are given out, and new substances such as carbon dioxide, water vapour and soot form.

subject: science
prompt_en: Milk left out on a hot day turns sour and forms lumps. Is this a physical or a chemical change? What is your evidence?
prompt_hi: Garmi ke din bahar chhoda doodh khatta ho ke phat jaata hai. Ye physical badlav hai ya chemical? Tumhara saboot kya hai?
answer: Chemical: there is a new sour smell and taste and lumps form, and it cannot be turned back into fresh milk.

subject: science
prompt_en: Think of a festival kitchen while sweets are being made. Name one physical change and one chemical change that happen there.
prompt_hi: Socho tyohaar ke din kitchen mein mithai ban rahi hai. Wahaan hone wala ek physical badlav aur ek chemical badlav batao.
answer: Physical: sugar dissolving in water for the syrup, ghee melting, dough being rolled. Chemical: dough or besan turning golden-brown when fried or roasted, or milk being made into chenna or paneer with lemon juice.

subject: science
prompt_en: Kunal says, 'When I stir salt into water, the salt melts.' Which word should he use, and how is it different from melting?
prompt_hi: Kunal kehta hai, 'Jab main namak paani mein hilaata hoon, toh namak pighal jaata hai.' Use kaunsa shabd use karna chahiye, aur wo pighalne se alag kaise hai?
answer: Dissolves. Dissolving is the salt spreading into the water to form a solution; melting is a solid turning into a liquid by heating, and salt needs a temperature of about 800 °C to melt.

subject: science
prompt_en: Sort these into a two-circle chart, 'physical' and 'chemical': freezing water into ice, cooking rice, folding a paper boat, a banana ripening, dissolving salt, toasting bread, blowing up a balloon.
prompt_hi: Inhe do gole wale chart mein baanto, 'physical' aur 'chemical': paani ka barf banna, chawal pakaana, kaagaz ki naav banana, kele ka pakna, namak gholna, bread toast karna, gubbara phulaana.
answer: Physical: freezing water, folding a paper boat, dissolving salt, blowing up a balloon. Chemical: cooking rice, a banana ripening, toasting bread.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to a younger child how to tell a physical change from a chemical change, using two examples from the kitchen.
prompt_hi: Ek chhote bachche ko kitchen ke do examples se samjhao ki physical aur chemical badlav mein farak kaise pehchaanein.
answer: Ask: has a new substance formed? If not, it is physical, like ice melting or sugar dissolving. If yes, with signs like a new colour, smell, gas, heat or light, it is chemical, like a roti browning or milk turning into curd.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: when water freezes in the freezer, is it a physical or a chemical change?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: jab freezer mein paani jamta hai, toh ye physical badlav hai ya chemical?
answer: Physical: it is still water, only in the solid state.

subject: science
prompt_en: Name the three things needed for a fire to burn.
prompt_hi: Aag jalne ke liye 3 zaroori cheezein batao.
answer: Fuel, oxygen (air) and enough heat to reach the ignition temperature.

subject: science
prompt_en: Think-only question; never try this yourself. In class, your teacher lights two identical candles and covers one with a small glass jar and the other with a big glass jar. Predict which flame goes out first, and why.
prompt_hi: Sirf sochne wala sawaal hai, ise khud kabhi try mat karna. Class mein teacher do ek jaisi mombattiyan jalaate hain aur ek ko chhote kaanch ke jar se aur doosri ko bade jar se dhak dete hain. Guess karo kaunsi lau pehle bujhegi, aur kyon?
answer: The one under the small jar goes out first, because it has less air, so its oxygen gets used up sooner.

subject: science
prompt_en: Think-only question. A piece of wood is burnt completely inside a strong sealed box from which nothing can escape, and the whole box is weighed before and after. Predict: will the total mass go down, stay the same or go up?
prompt_hi: Sirf sochne wala sawaal. Lakdi ka ek tukda ek mazboot band dibbe mein poora jala diya jaata hai jahaan se kuch bhi bahar nahi nikal sakta, aur poore dibbe ko pehle aur baad mein tola jaata hai. Guess karo: kul wazan ghatega, utna hi rahega ya badhega?
answer: It stays the same: the wood and the oxygen it used turn into ash, smoke and gases that are all still inside the box; nothing is destroyed. In an open fire the gases escape, which is why the ash left behind is lighter.

subject: science
prompt_en: Think-only question. In a science video, a paper cup full of water is held over a steady flame. Predict: will the paper cup catch fire before the water boils?
prompt_hi: Sirf sochne wala sawaal. Ek science video mein paani se bhara kaagaz ka cup ek sthir lau ke upar pakda jaata hai. Guess karo: kya paani ubalne se pehle kaagaz ka cup jal jaayega?
answer: No. The water keeps taking heat away from the paper, so the paper stays below its ignition temperature while there is water in it.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why does fanning a sigri or a chulha make it burn more strongly?
prompt_hi: Sigri ya chulhe ko pankha jhalne se wo zyada tez kyon jalta hai?
answer: Fanning pushes more fresh, oxygen-rich air to the fuel, so it burns faster and gives more heat and light.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why must water never be thrown on burning oil in a kadhai, or on an electrical fire?
prompt_hi: Kadhai ke jalte tel pe ya bijli ki aag pe kabhi paani kyon nahi daalna chahiye?
answer: Oil floats on water and the water turns to steam explosively, splashing burning oil and spreading the fire; water also conducts electricity and could give a shock. Adults should turn off the gas or power and cover the fire to cut off air.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare the rusting of an iron nail with the burning of a matchstick. Give one way they are the same and two ways they are different.
prompt_hi: Lohe ki keel ke jung lagne aur maachis ki teeli ke jalne ki tulna karo. Ek samaanta aur do farak batao.
answer: Same: both are chemical changes in which a substance combines with oxygen. Different: rusting is slow (days to weeks) and needs water, with no flame or light; burning is fast and gives out heat and light.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why do petrol pumps keep buckets of sand, and why do firefighters cover some fires with foam?
prompt_hi: Petrol pump pe ret ki baaltiyan kyon rakhi jaati hain, aur fire-fighters kuch aag ko foam se kyon dhakte hain?
answer: Sand and foam cover the burning fuel and cut off its oxygen, so the fire goes out; water is not safe on burning petrol because petrol floats on water.

subject: science
prompt_en: In some states, farmers burn leftover crop straw (parali) in the fields. Using what you know about combustion, explain where the straw's matter goes and why cities far away get smoky air.
prompt_hi: Kuch rajyon mein kisaan khet mein bachi parali jalaate hain. Combustion ke baare mein jo jaante ho uske hisaab se samjhao ki parali ka padarth kahaan jaata hai aur door ke shehron ki hawa dhuaan-dhuaan kyon ho jaati hai.
answer: Burning turns the straw into carbon dioxide, water vapour, smoke particles and ash; the gases and smoke rise into the air and winds carry them to cities, where the smoke pollutes the air.

subject: science
prompt_en: Pinky says, 'After a bonfire, the ash is so light, so most of the wood was destroyed into nothing.' What is the mistake?
prompt_hi: Pinky kehti hai, 'Alaav ke baad raakh itni halki hoti hai, matlab zyadatar lakdi khatam ho ke kuch nahi bachi.' Galti kya hai?
answer: The wood's matter was not destroyed; most of it turned into gases (carbon dioxide and water vapour) and smoke that went into the air. Only a small part was left as ash.

subject: science
prompt_en: Draw a fire triangle and label its three sides. Next to each side, draw one way of removing it to put a fire out.
prompt_hi: Ek fire triangle banao aur uski teeno bhujaon pe label lagao. Har bhuja ke paas aag bujhaane ke liye use hataane ka ek tareeka banao.
answer: Fuel: remove the fuel, for example turn off the gas. Oxygen: cut off air with a lid, sand or a fire blanket. Heat: cool it with water (only for wood, paper or cloth fires).
